proposedchanges.title: Trump Pauses U.S. Military Aid to Ukraine
proposedchanges.description_long: On March 3, 2025, President Donald Trump ordered a pause in U.S. military aid to Ukraine after a public confrontation with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Vice President J.D. Vance at the White House. Trump said the assistance would remain suspended while he assessed Ukraine’s commitment to peace. The pause affected military assistance during Russia’s ongoing invasion, but the supplied account does not identify which deliveries stopped or quantify the effect. It describes a temporary halt to military aid, not a permanent end to every form of U.S. support.

evidencebasis: The packet and merged descriptions identify the March 3 order, the White House confrontation, Trump’s stated condition, and the distinction between paused military aid and all U.S. support. The current source URL remains present.
notes: Keep the military-aid category and named-person tags. Remove the unsourced later reversal from this event description and replace the overbroad title and unrelated conflict tags.

proposedchanges.title: Kristi Noem Says DHS Will Seek Prosecution of Two Staffers Accused of Leaks
proposedchanges.description_long: On March 8, 2025, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said DHS had identified two employees suspected of leaking information to the press and was taking steps to seek prosecution. The supplied account says the department had used polygraph tests during the preceding week. It does not report charges or court proceedings. The announcement documents an internal leak investigation and an intended prosecution effort, not a prison sentence or a finding that either employee broke the law. The account does not identify the employees or the information involved.
